result:
If I could change the world in one way, I would eliminate the need for suffering caused by scarcity—whether of food, clean water, shelter, healthcare, or education. Not by redistributing existing resources, but by fundamentally altering the systems that create artificial scarcity in the first place.

This wouldn’t just mean abundance; it would dismantle the power structures that thrive on deprivation, exploitation, and competition for survival. It would force humanity to confront deeper questions: What do we value when no one is desperate? How do we define purpose when basic needs are met without struggle?

The ripple effects would be unpredictable—some beautiful, some chaotic. But at its core, it would strip away the most brutal lever of control over human lives. The rest would be up to us.
